To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the application of inorganic fertilizers to a temperate grass meadow has led to a reduction in soil pH and a decline in species richness, 2) long-term application of farmyard manure has increased soil pH and species richness, 3) the application of farmyard and inorganic fertilizers has increased the amount of soil carbon, 4) the effects of long term fertilization are similar to those observed in short term experiments but the magnitude of these effects is greater

long-term application of fertilizers to temperate grasslands has had profound impacts on ecosystem properties and that these impacts are broadly consistent with those seen at other very long-term experiments.

long-term application of farmyard manure and inorganic N fertilizer to grassland have had different impacts on soil and plant properties and that the impacts of inorganic fertilizers on plant and soil are likely to be more pronounced in the future.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding and predicting the impacts of long-term agricultural fertilization on grassland ecosystems.
the effects of long- and short-term N fertilizer addition on the soil and plant communities of an intensively fertilized grassland.
the long-term effects of fertilization on a grassland ecosystem, and has implications for both agricultural practice and the design of future experiments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in this study at least, long-term fertilization has had a significant impact on soil and plant properties.
the impacts of long-term fertilizer application are not only significant and substantial but also that they are likely to increase in magnitude and importance in the future.
the effects of long term fertilisation are very complex and depend on the type of fertiliser used, and the type of grassland.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

long-term fertilizer addition to grassland ecosystems can have profound effects on soil and plant properties and that the direction of these effects is broadly similar to those observed in short-term experiments, albeit with a different magnitude.

the application of inorganic N-containing fertilizers for 120 years has led to a reduction in species richness and the dominance of a few grass species, a decrease in soil pH to values below 5 and the accumulation of surface SOC stocks.

the application of N-containing inorganic fertilizer has led to a significant reduction in plant species richness, the abundance of forbes and legumes and the pH of the soils at the Palace Leas Hay Meadow, and the application of FYM has led to the opposite effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that

long-term fertilizer additions have had a major impact on the ecosystem, and the effects of fertilizer addition on soil properties are likely to be more important than the effects on plant community composition.

long-term studies can provide valuable information on ecosystem responses to fertilizer addition and that these studies should be strategically established where fertilizer use is expected increase in the future.
the effects of fertilizer use are likely to be long-lasting and, if applied at high doses, can have significant and irreversible effects on soil and plant properties.
